definition: an area of ground where dead people are buried

collocations.example: She rests beside her husband in the local cemetery.
We visit the cemetery to honor our grandparents.

definition: to remove parts of a book, film, or message considered unacceptable

collocations.example: The government tried to censor the news reports.
Prison officials censor the letters that inmates send.

definition: an official count of all the people living in a country

collocations.example: Census data shows the population is steadily growing.
The government will conduct a census next year.

definition: an official document that proves a particular fact is true

collocations.example: You need your birth certificate to apply for a passport.
They framed their marriage certificate and hung it up.

definition: to state officially that something is true or meets a standard

collocations.example: Officials must certify the results of the election.
Auditors certify the accounts as true and fair.

definition: an expensive sparkling white wine, often drunk to celebrate

collocations.example: They ordered a bottle of champagne to celebrate.
He opened the champagne when the deal closed.

definition: a very senior government official, or the head of government in some countries

collocations.example: The German chancellor met with other European leaders.
The chancellor announced new tax cuts in the budget.

definition: a state of complete disorder and confusion

collocations.example: The country descended into chaos after the war.
The airport was in chaos after the heavy snow.

definition: a small church or a room used for Christian worship

collocations.example: They were married in the college chapel.
The hospital has a small chapel for visitors.

definition: a professional cook, especially the main cook in a restaurant

collocations.example: Try this dish created by our head chef.
She trained for years to become a professional chef.

definition: the science that studies substances and how they react together

collocations.example: She studied chemistry at university for three years.
He failed his organic chemistry exam last semester.

definition: the part of the face below the mouth

collocations.example: He was starting to develop a double chin.
She rubbed her chin thoughtfully before answering.

definition: a group of people who sing together, often in a church or school

collocations.example: She sings in the school choir every week.
The church choir rehearses on Thursday evenings.

definition: to be unable to breathe because something blocks the throat

collocations.example: She began to choke on a piece of bread.
He nearly choked to death on a fish bone.

definition: a fatty substance in the blood that can harm health in large amounts

collocations.example: I want to lower my cholesterol level through diet.
Fatty foods can lead to high cholesterol.

definition: (of an illness) lasting a long time and hard to cure

collocations.example: He suffers from a chronic illness that needs daily medication.
She has lived with chronic pain for many years.

definition: a written record of events arranged in the order they happened

collocations.example: The book is a chronicle of the war years.
She kept a detailed chronicle of her travels.

definition: a thick, solid piece of something

collocations.example: He cut a chunk of cheese for the guests.
Break the chocolate into chunks before melting it.

definition: a building where people go to watch films

collocations.example: We go to the cinema every Friday night.
The film is showing at our local cinema.

definition: relating to a town or city and the duties of its citizens

collocations.example: Voting is an important civic duty for everyone.
Residents take great civic pride in their town.

definition: to fight or disagree strongly with someone

collocations.example: Protesters clashed with police outside the building.
The two parties clashed over the new budget.

definition: the arrangement of things into groups by their type or features

collocations.example: The library uses a clear classification system for books.
Biologists study the classification of plants and animals.

definition: to arrange things into groups according to their type

collocations.example: Experts classify the whale as a mammal, not a fish.
We classify the data into three main groups.

definition: a heavy, sticky type of earth used to make pots and bricks

collocations.example: The tiles on the roof are made of clay.
She baked the stew slowly in a clay pot.

definition: a person who keeps records or serves customers in an office or shop

collocations.example: The bank clerk counted the money carefully.
The desk clerk gave us the room keys.

definition: to press a button on a computer mouse to choose something

collocations.example: Click on the icon to open the program.
Double-click the file to start the installation.

definition: to hold on to something or someone very tightly

collocations.example: The frightened child clung to her mother's arm.
He managed to cling on to the rope.

definition: to make an exact genetic copy of a living thing

collocations.example: Scientists were the first to clone an animal.
Researchers managed to clone a single gene.

definition: the permanent closing of a business, factory, or other place

collocations.example: The small village school may face closure next year.
The factory closure left hundreds of workers jobless.

definition: the part of a vehicle used to change gear

collocations.example: The mechanic said the car needs a new clutch.
Press the clutch pedal before you change gear.

definition: a box in which a dead body is buried or cremated

collocations.example: They buried him in a simple wooden coffin.
Six men carried the coffin into the church.

definition: relating to thinking, learning, and understanding

collocations.example: The test measures the cognitive ability of each student.
Lack of sleep can affect your cognitive function.

definition: clear, logical, and well organized

collocations.example: She presented a clear and coherent argument.
The company lacks a coherent strategy for growth.

definition: the part of a shirt or coat that fits around the neck

collocations.example: He loosened his shirt collar in the heat.
The guard grabbed him by the collar.

definition: a senior officer in the army

collocations.example: Her father was an army colonel for decades.
The speech was given by a retired colonel.

definition: intended to make people laugh; funny

collocations.example: He is best known as a comic actor.
The clown provided some comic relief during the play.

definition: a person who describes or comments on events, often on television or radio

collocations.example: He works as a sports commentator for the channel.
The political commentator analyzed the election results.

definition: a raw material or product that can be bought and sold

collocations.example: Global commodity prices rose sharply last month.
Clean water is a valuable commodity in the desert.

definition: to travel regularly between home and work

collocations.example: She commutes to work by train every day.
Many people commute long distances to find good jobs.

definition: small and neatly fitted into a limited space

collocations.example: They rented a compact car for the city trip.
The phone has a slim and compact design.

definition: measured or judged by comparing one thing with another

collocations.example: They published a comparative study of the two systems.
The country has a comparative advantage in farming.

definition: able to be used or to work together without problems

collocations.example: The new software is compatible with older computers.
These two systems are fully compatible with each other.

definition: to force someone to do something

collocations.example: The law can compel employers to pay fair wages.
She felt compelled to tell him the truth.

definition: the ability to do something well

collocations.example: The exam tests the professional competence of nurses.
She performs her job with a high level of competence.

definition: to collect information and arrange it into a list or report

collocations.example: We are trying to compile a list of volunteers.
It took weeks to compile the annual report.

definition: to add to something so that it becomes better or more complete

collocations.example: The two colors complement each other beautifully.
A light wine will complement the meal nicely.

definition: the act of obeying a rule, order, or request

collocations.example: Inspectors checked compliance with the safety rules.
Managers must ensure compliance with company policy.

definition: to act according to a rule, order, or request

collocations.example: All staff must comply with the new regulations.
They refused to comply with the court order.

definition: to understand something fully

collocations.example: Many people fail to comprehend the scale of the problem.
The vastness of space is hard to comprehend.

definition: to press or squeeze something into a smaller space

collocations.example: This program can compress large amounts of data.
The waste is tightly compressed to save space.

definition: a trick used to cheat someone out of money

collocations.example: A con man tricked her out of her savings.
The so-called bargain was just a big con.

definition: to hide something so that it cannot be seen or known

collocations.example: He tried to conceal the truth from his family.
She could barely conceal her disappointment at the news.

definition: to admit, often unwillingly, that something is true

collocations.example: He was forced to concede that he was wrong.
She reluctantly conceded that the plan had failed.

definition: something you allow or give up to end a disagreement

collocations.example: Neither side was willing to make a concession.
The union won a major concession on wages.

definition: meant to be kept secret and shared only with certain people

collocations.example: Employees must not share confidential information with outsiders.
Please keep the contents of this letter strictly confidential.

definition: to set up equipment or software so it works in a certain way

collocations.example: The technician will configure the software for you.
You can configure the settings in the main menu.

definition: to behave or operate according to rules or standards

collocations.example: The product must conform to safety standards.
Teenagers often refuse to conform to their parents' rules.

definition: to tell someone you are pleased about their success or good luck

collocations.example: I want to congratulate you on your promotion.
The coach warmly congratulated the winning team.

definition: to come together and form a group

collocations.example: Young people congregate in the square every evening.
Fans congregated around the entrance to the stadium.

definition: the inner sense that tells you whether your actions are right or wrong

collocations.example: He had a guilty conscience after telling the lie.
She returned the money to keep a clear conscience.

definition: general agreement among a group of people

collocations.example: The committee failed to reach a consensus on the issue.
There is a broad consensus among scientists on this.

definition: the quality of always behaving or performing in the same way

collocations.example: The team's main weakness is a lack of consistency.
The chain works hard to maintain consistency across its restaurants.

definition: to give comfort to someone who is sad or disappointed

collocations.example: She tried to console her friend after the loss.
You can console yourself with the thought you tried.

definition: to make something such as power or a position stronger and more secure

collocations.example: The new leader moved quickly to consolidate power.
The company consolidated its position in the market.

definition: a secret plan by a group to do something harmful or illegal

collocations.example: They uncovered a conspiracy to overthrow the government.
He believed there was a conspiracy against him.

definition: an area and its voters that a politician represents

collocations.example: Unemployment is very high in her constituency.
He represents a large rural constituency in parliament.

definition: to make something dirty or harmful by adding a dangerous substance

collocations.example: Chemicals from the factory contaminate the local water supply.
Leaking fuel can contaminate the soil for years.

definition: to think carefully about doing something

collocations.example: She began to contemplate leaving her job.
He is seriously contemplating a move abroad next year.

definition: a strong feeling that someone or something is worthless

collocations.example: She looked at him with utter contempt.
He has nothing but contempt for dishonest people.

definition: a group of people who represent one country or organization

collocations.example: The largest contingent of athletes came from Japan.
A small contingent from the local club attended.

definition: opposite in nature or direction to something else

collocations.example: Contrary to popular belief, many cats dislike milk.
She holds a contrary view on the matter.

definition: the quality of being useful and easy, causing little trouble

collocations.example: Many shoppers use credit cards for convenience.
Customers enjoy the convenience of shopping online from home.

definition: useful and easy, causing little difficulty or trouble

collocations.example: Please call back at a more convenient time.
The hotel is very convenient for the airport.

definition: the process of changing something from one form into another

collocations.example: The conversion of the barn into a house took months.
No data conversion is needed between the two systems.

definition: a soft reddish-brown metal that conducts heat and electricity well

collocations.example: Electricians use copper wire because it conducts well.
Water flows through the old copper pipes.

definition: the legal right to control the use of a creative work

collocations.example: The company broke copyright law by copying the songs.
The author still owns the copyright to her books.

definition: a length of wire covered in plastic used to connect electrical equipment

collocations.example: Plug the power cord into the wall socket.
He used an extension cord to reach the outlet.

definition: a tall plant grown for its yellow grain, also called maize

collocations.example: The old mill was used to grind corn.
The farmer planted a large field of corn.

definition: an organized group of people who work together, often in the military

collocations.example: He served in the Marine Corps for ten years.
The press corps followed the president everywhere.

definition: a set of clothes worn to look like someone else or for a special event

collocations.example: The children wore masks to the costume party.
The actress had four costume changes during the show.

definition: a long, soft seat for more than one person; a sofa

collocations.example: They sat on the couch watching television all evening.
She bought a brown leather couch for the living room.

definition: a person or thing with the same role or position as another

collocations.example: The minister met his counterpart from France.
The female bird is duller than its male counterpart.

definition: a sudden, often violent seizure of government power

collocations.example: The president was removed in a military coup.
The generals tried to stage a coup last night.

definition: polite behavior and good manners toward others

collocations.example: The staff treated every guest with great courtesy.
It is common courtesy to hold the door open.

definition: able to be believed; convincing

collocations.example: He could not give a credible explanation for the delay.
The jury found her to be a credible witness.

definition: a detailed assessment that examines the good and bad points of something

collocations.example: She wrote a sharp critique of the new policy.
The professor offered a detailed critique of my essay.

definition: in a natural or raw state; not yet processed or refined

collocations.example: Crude oil is the world's most important commodity.
The factory produces thousands of tons of crude steel.

definition: to break slowly into small pieces

collocations.example: The old walls are slowly crumbling into dust.
The dry cake began to crumble as she cut it.

definition: the hard outer part of bread or a baked pastry

collocations.example: The fresh bread had a lovely crispy crust.
She rolled out the dough to make the pie crust.

definition: a solid shape with six equal square sides

collocations.example: She dropped an ice cube into her drink.
He added a sugar cube to his coffee.

definition: a small religious group with beliefs most people consider extreme

collocations.example: She joined a religious cult when she was young.
The cult leader controlled every part of their lives.

definition: to prepare land and grow crops on it

collocations.example: Farmers cultivate the land along the river valley.
They cultivate rice and beans on the small farm.

definition: an evil wish or spell meant to bring someone bad luck

collocations.example: She believed someone had put a curse on her family.
The villagers feared they were under a curse.

definition: the state of being kept in prison, especially while awaiting trial

collocations.example: The suspect is being held in police custody.
He was released from custody the next day.

definition: believing that people act only for selfish reasons; distrustful

collocations.example: She is very cynical about the film industry.
He has a deeply cynical view of politicians.

definition: a strong barrier built across a river to hold back water

collocations.example: The government plans to build a dam across the river.
The dam burst and flooded the villages below.

definition: to go or run somewhere very quickly

collocations.example: I'm sorry, but I really have to dash now.
She dashed off to catch the early train.

definition: a time or date by which something must be finished

collocations.example: The team worked late to meet the deadline.
If we miss the deadline, we lose the contract.

definition: unable to hear, either fully or partly

collocations.example: Their youngest child was born deaf.
After the accident he became partially deaf.

definition: a first public appearance or performance

collocations.example: Their debut album was a huge commercial success.
She will make her debut on the national team.
